theme: How much data until the model is good enough
title: How Much Data Until It's Good Enough? — Forecasting Past the Floor
strategies: trivial: predict the constant mean of the observed training errors, ignoring the decaying trend -> reproduces the checker baseline ~0.1

greedy: fit a plain power law (no floor) via log-log OLS pooling every visible point; this is forced toward 0 as n grows, but true error never drops below the irreducible floor, and pooling blends the steep early-burst exponent with the true shallow one -> badly wrong at held-out scale

strong: posit floor + power-law, profile out the exponent via grid search with a closed-form linear regression for (floor, amplitude) at each candidate exponent, and search over largest-n suffixes of the training points to find the self-consistent subset (rejecting early-burst contamination) with the cleanest curvature fit -> extrapolates correctly
headroom above strong: sharper floor estimation under measurement noise (e.g. iteratively reweighted fits, better break-point localisation) to push held-out MSE further toward the noise floor
